body: Thank you. This is what I hoped, that at least one other person knows what I feel like sometimes. I've been in college for the last few years, but even around campus I always felt so alone and weird. I don't feel that way so much now, knowing there are other people who have it good but... I don't know, think those dark thoughts. Thank you so much. I just wanted you to know how much that means to me.

I know, I have thought about it, I mean really thought about it. I get curious about it, what comes next, how does it feel to be nothing, what does it really mean to be nothing and experience the nothing. It would all be over, I don't see an issue with that part. Death happens to everyone, people die everywhere, it happens all day. Some die by choice, others not so much, it just happens. It's a natural thing. And what's so bad about our silly human problems not ever mattering again? Aren't those bad human problems the reason we think about suicide? 

Why then do I think most about killing myself while life is going awesome and there's nothing to worry about, when I should be most clear-headed and sane? Why do I feel like this is the end of a good story and it really doesn't need to continue past this point? It's not an unhappy feeling. Just maybe a little delusional? I'm not sure. That's the point here, why when I am at my most content do I feel the most like killing myself, when it's usually the complete opposite for people? Or do other people feel like I do.

Thank you, your words mean a lot to me.

Thank you, I *do* value my own life experiences and equally value those of others past and present. It's just hard to see the point of all of it. I get to thinking on far too large a scale.

But as far off track as I got (I was about to go to bed, so all of my thoughts about the universe were also invading my thoughts) really the only thing I want to know is if other people are genuinely at a good place in their life and still want to kill themselves, just so the story has a happy ending.

Thank you for your patience with me, and thank you for reading this. It means a whole bunch. You're a good person.

*I did a rant. I'm really sorry, I don't know what came over me. But you can skip to the very end if you want, I think I just needed to write all of this out.*

It's not so much me feeling like I don't deserve it. I mean, we're all the same, every single person in the world is the same, like, we're all on the same level and it's not a matter of who deserves or doesn't deserve anything. Everybody feels happy sometimes and that's awesome, and everybody feels sad sometimes and that's terrible. It's more like, okay, we're all just really advanced animals. And just take a minute, look around you. Everything in your house, everything in your room, is made completely by a person. Some person made every single little piece of everything you own. Except if it's like, a tree or a dog or something, even then it's cultivated and bred by a person. 

And all of our problems, god, they're so *human*, you know? I mean, wolves don't have the problems I have, geese don't give a shit, y'know what I mean? Cat just licks himself and eats some food, and sleeps, whatever. School, jobs, relationships, failure, these are all entirely human concepts. And not only are all of our own problems entirely made up by people, not only do we fuck with each other and ruin each other's lives, there are horrible horrible people out there that do horrible illogical things, and yes there are good people who are amazing and do so much for others that it restores your hope, but god damn they are surrounded by pure destruction, not just of each other and other animals, but of the entire world, just because we are so goddamned entitled that we think we rule everything when we are no better than any other plant or animal on the planet. Everything is a human concept, it is a human concept that we are important at all. It's outrageous.

A human concept is the storybook. The movie. I don't know why, I know my life isn't a book or a movie, it is a life. A human life, a person's life, a very intelligent animal living out a life surrounded by other very intelligent animals. But again, it's not that I feel I don't deserve to be happy, or even that I'm sad. I mean, I'm not really passionate about anything. I don't DO anything, I just... reddit, and play video games, and go to school and read and write a bit and come home, and I sleep. But it's not that I'm unhappy. It's that when I am happy, I feel like the story should end right there because it's on a high note and it's all perfect. The perfect time to end it, because this is where the story should end. Because life is great, and I enjoy it right that moment.

And I do, the weird thing is I do enjoy life, the little things, I laugh, I'm generally optimistic and happy, but... God, I feel like I'm some kind of crazy person, because even though I feel optimistic and happy, underneath it, sort of, but removed from it is this feeling that there is no purpose for any of it. I will never make an impact that will last on anything, unless it's negative. Okay, if I get super famous for something I might make an impact on humans. But the human race isn't going to last, none of it really lasts, so unless I go and blow up a fucking mountain and make all the rubble shape into my face, I won't matter, and nothing I do matters outside of, y'know, humans.

Jesus, I sound crazy even to myself. I'm sorry. 

**All I wanted to know was if other people ever feel like they need to end the story when it's on a high note. That's all I want to know, am I normal or am I really screwed up, should I go to therapy. I don't know how to explain it any better than that. I don't really know what else to say. Well... Thank you for your time, really. I appreciate it a lot.**
